$comment: Illustrative flows over the platform graph. Each step animates one or more edges (source>target; prefix '<' to animate against the arrow) and shows a caption. Steps describe how the system works; they are not a recording — the real /make run is the replay.

steps.caption: The console opens from the laptop or the phone, inside the private tailnet — it is not reachable from the internet.
The console calls the API over loopback. API keys exist only on the server.
Rules and a local classifier mark the request as sensitive, so policy keeps it on the local 7B model.
The answer streams back from the CPU box. Nothing went to the cloud.
The run log records the decision, route and latency — never the text.
I start `/make <intent>` in an agent session on the server.
The executor finds the matching procedure and writes a plan.
A separate verifier with a fresh context checks the plan against policies and permissions: GO or STOP.
After the change it runs deterministic checks on the services: PASS or FAIL.
A pull request for review (merging is human-only) and an entry in the session log.
